reading.title: Why Old Batteries Need Their Own Collection
reading.intro_zh: 本文不复述 Percy Buttons 的故事，而是顺着“每月固定来收旧电池的社区志愿者”这一主题，介绍一个真实的环境问题：废旧电池为什么必须单独回收、不能扔进普通垃圾桶。内容改编自美国环境保护署（EPA）的权威科普资料。

source.title: Used Household Batteries / Used Lithium-Ion Batteries

passage: When a community volunteer calls at your door once a month to collect old batteries, the routine can look unnecessary. In fact, it solves a genuine and growing hazard. The rechargeable lithium-ion batteries that power our phones, laptops, and electric toothbrushes are not ordinary rubbish. According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, these batteries should never be thrown into household garbage or tossed into a curbside recycling bin. The reason is mechanical as much as chemical: once a battery enters the waste stream, it is likely to be crushed or punctured by the heavy sorting equipment at a processing facility. A damaged cell can short-circuit, overheat, and ignite, and even a battery that seems completely dead may still store enough energy to start a fire.

These fires are far from theoretical. They endanger waste-collection workers, damage expensive recycling machinery, and have repeatedly broken out at facilities that were built only to handle paper, plastic, metal, and glass. To reduce the danger, the EPA advises consumers to insulate each battery before disposal, either by placing it in a separate plastic bag or by covering its terminals with non-conductive tape. The batteries should then be taken to a certified electronics recycler or a household hazardous-waste collection point rather than the ordinary bin.

Beyond preventing fires, careful recycling has a second purpose. Lithium-ion batteries contain critical minerals such as cobalt, lithium, and graphite, materials that are difficult and costly to extract from the earth. Recovering them conserves natural resources and reduces the pollution generated by mining. Seen this way, the monthly visitor with her collection box is not an eccentric local character but a small, deliberate part of a much larger system.

questions.question: What is the main point the passage makes about used lithium-ion batteries?
options: They are cheaper to replace than to recycle.
They should be kept at home rather than discarded.
They must be collected separately because they are hazardous and contain valuable materials.
They are no longer used in modern electronic devices.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕“锂电池既危险又含有宝贵材料，所以必须单独回收”展开，这是中心论点。其他选项都不是文章主旨。

questions.question: According to the EPA, where should lithium-ion batteries NOT be placed?
options: In household garbage or a curbside recycling bin.
At a certified electronics recycler.
Inside a separate plastic bag before disposal.
At a household hazardous-waste collection point.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中明确说锂电池绝不能扔进生活垃圾或路边回收桶（never be thrown into household garbage or tossed into a curbside recycling bin）。其余三项都是文章建议的正确做法。

questions.question: Why does putting a battery into the ordinary waste stream create a fire risk?
options: Because batteries react chemically with paper and glass.
Because recycling facilities deliberately overheat them.
Because workers refuse to handle them carefully.
Because heavy sorting equipment can crush or puncture the battery, causing it to short-circuit and ignite.
questions.explanation_zh: 文章解释，电池进入垃圾流后会被沉重的分拣设备压碎或刺穿，受损电芯会短路、过热并起火，这是起火的根本原因。

questions.question: What can be inferred about the monthly volunteer who collects batteries?
options: She is wasting her time on an unnecessary chore.
Her routine work supports a wider effort to prevent fires and recover scarce materials.
She is mainly interested in selling the batteries for profit.
She collects batteries only because the law forces her to.
questions.explanation_zh: 结尾指出这位每月来访者“是更大系统中一个有意为之的小环节”，可推断她的工作支撑着防火和回收稀缺材料这一更广泛的努力。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "insulate" (in "insulate each battery before disposal") most nearly means to
options: throw the battery away quickly.
recharge the battery fully.
cover or isolate the battery so its terminals cannot make contact.
label the battery with a warning sign.
questions.explanation_zh: 下文用“放进单独的塑料袋”或“用非导电胶带盖住电极”来解释 insulate，因此它在此指把电池隔离起来，让电极无法接触。

writing.intro_zh: 今天的仿写仍抓住 Lesson 6 最值得迁移的五个结构：刚搬到某地、向某人要某物、作为回报、后来邻居解释、以及 once a month 表示固定频率。这一轮请把句子写得更复杂、更接近真实社区生活的语境，同时记住安全边界：孩子不要独自开门。

patterns.title: have just moved to ...
patterns.source: I have just moved to a house in Bridge Street.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 have just moved to 说明刚搬到一个新地方，所以还不了解周围的人和规矩。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：你刚搬到一个陌生城市或社区，因此还无法判断当地的人际关系或某些约定俗成的规矩。
patterns.sample: I have just moved to an unfamiliar district, so I still cannot tell which neighbours are trustworthy and which routines are local.
patterns.tip_zh: have just moved to 后面接地点；后半句可以自然说明“我为什么不知道”。

patterns.title: asked me for ...
patterns.source: He asked me for a meal and a glass of beer.
patterns.focus_zh: asked me for 表示“向我请求某物”，后面直接接想要的东西。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：某位工作人员或志愿者出于一个明确的环保或公益目的，向你要一件具体而合理的物品。
patterns.sample: The recycling volunteer politely asked me for the used batteries that had been gathering dust in our kitchen drawer for months.
patterns.tip_zh: asked me for 后面接名词，不要写成 asked me to for。

patterns.title: In return for this, ...
patterns.source: In return for this, the beggar stood on his head and sang songs.
patterns.focus_zh: In return for this 放在句首，表示前后两件事是一种交换或回报。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：别人向你提供了帮助或信息，作为回报，你用一个具体且对等的行动予以回应。
patterns.sample: In return for this, the volunteer left us a printed schedule explaining exactly when hazardous waste would be collected each season.
patterns.tip_zh: 逗号后面写具体动作；动作要和前面的帮助形成清楚的交换关系。

patterns.title: Later a neighbour told me about ...
patterns.source: Later a neighbour told me about him.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 Later 把故事推到后面，再让 neighbour 解释一个新来的人不知道的情况。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：后来邻居向你解释了某个你原本误解的社区运作机制或长期惯例。
must_include: Later a neighbour told me about
patterns.sample: Later a neighbour told me about the quiet system behind these monthly visits, which I had wrongly assumed was just a personal habit.
patterns.tip_zh: about 后面接解释对象，比如 the visitor, the shop, the routine。

patterns.title: calls at ... once a month
patterns.source: He calls at every house in the street once a month.
patterns.focus_zh: calls at 表示“到某处拜访或停留”，once a month 表示“每月一次”，合起来写固定的社区、学校或家庭习惯。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个人或一支队伍每月一次到某处，执行一项需要专门处理的固定任务。
patterns.sample: A trained volunteer calls at every building in our district once a month to collect items that must never enter ordinary household rubbish.
patterns.tip_zh: 频率短语 once a month 通常放在句末，让读者最后看到这个 routine。
